lessons.title: What is Gemini?
lessons.subtitle: Meet Google's most capable AI — and why it matters for you

cards.headline: Google's AI is already everywhere
cards.body: Gemini powers Google Search, Gmail, Docs, Maps, and your phone. Over 2 billion people interact with Gemini-powered features daily — most without realising it. Today you'll meet it properly.
cards.statLabel: daily users touched by Gemini AI

cards.headline: What Gemini actually is
cards.body: Gemini is Google's family of AI models — it can understand and generate text, images, code, audio, and video. Think of it as a brilliant assistant that can read, write, see, and reason.
bullets: Built by Google DeepMind — the team behind AlphaGo
Multimodal from day one — text, images, audio, video
Integrated into Google products you already use
Available free (with a powerful paid tier too)

cards.headline: Gemini vs. ChatGPT vs. Claude
cards.body: Each AI has strengths. Gemini's superpower is its deep integration with Google's ecosystem — Search, Gmail, Docs, YouTube, Maps, and more. It also excels at multimodal tasks (images + text together).
bullets: Gemini: Best Google integration, multimodal, real-time info
ChatGPT: Largest ecosystem of plugins and tools
Claude: Strongest at long-form reasoning and writing
Smart users learn to use the right tool for the right job

cards.headline: Where to find Gemini
cards.body: You can access Gemini in multiple places — no installation needed for most of them.
bullets: gemini.google.com — the main web app (free)
Google app on your phone — tap the Gemini tab
Inside Gmail, Docs, Sheets — the "Help me write" button
Android phones — replace Google Assistant with Gemini

cards.headline: Your first look
cards.body: Open gemini.google.com in a new tab (or the Google app on your phone). Sign in with your Google account. Don't type anything yet — just look around. Notice the suggestion chips, the text box, and the image upload button. Tomorrow you'll have your first real conversation.

quiz.question: What makes Gemini different from other AI assistants like ChatGPT?
options: Deep integration with Google products and multimodal capabilities
quiz.explanation: Gemini's key differentiator is its deep integration with Google's ecosystem (Search, Gmail, Docs, etc.) and its native multimodal capabilities — understanding text, images, audio, and video together.

quiz.question: Gemini can understand images, not just text.
quiz.explanation: Correct! Gemini is multimodal from the ground up — it can process and reason about text, images, audio, and video.

quiz.question: Which is NOT a way to access Gemini?
options: The Google app on your phone
quiz.explanation: Gemini is integrated into Google products (Docs, Gmail, Sheets) and the Google app — but not Microsoft Word, which uses Microsoft's own Copilot AI.

lessons.title: Your First Conversation
lessons.subtitle: If you can type, you can use Gemini

cards.headline: It's just like texting a really smart friend
cards.body: There's no coding, no special syntax, no learning curve. You type what you want in plain English, and Gemini responds. The hardest part? Realising how easy it actually is.
cards.statLabel: to get your first useful answer

cards.headline: How to start a conversation
cards.body: Go to gemini.google.com and type anything in the text box. That's it. No setup, no configuration, no account creation beyond your Google login.
bullets: Type naturally — like you're asking a colleague
Be specific about what you want ("Write a thank-you email to my client")
You can ask follow-up questions in the same chat
Hit the + button to start a fresh conversation anytime

cards.headline: 5 starter prompts that always work
cards.body: Not sure what to say? Try these — they're designed to show you what Gemini can do in under 60 seconds.
bullets: "Explain [topic] like I'm 10 years old"
"Write a professional email declining a meeting politely"
"Give me 5 dinner ideas using chicken and rice"
"Summarise the pros and cons of working from home"
"Help me plan a weekend trip to [city]"

cards.headline: Understanding Gemini's responses
cards.body: Gemini responds in formatted text — with headings, bullet points, and sometimes even tables. You can copy, edit, or ask it to try again.
bullets: Click "Show drafts" to see alternative versions
Use the thumbs up/down to give feedback
Click the copy button to grab the text instantly
Say "Make it shorter" or "Make it more formal" to adjust

cards.headline: Have your first conversation
cards.body: Open Gemini and try this prompt: "I'm learning to use AI for the first time. Give me 3 ways you can help me today based on things most people do every day." Read the response, then ask one follow-up question. Congratulations — you're now an AI user!

quiz.question: What do you need to start using Gemini?
options: A paid subscription and special software
A Google account and a web browser
quiz.explanation: All you need is a Google account and a web browser (or the Google app). Gemini is free to use at gemini.google.com.

quiz.question: You can ask Gemini follow-up questions in the same conversation.
quiz.explanation: Yes! Gemini remembers context within a conversation, so you can ask follow-ups, clarify, or build on previous answers.

quiz.question: What does "Show drafts" do in Gemini?
options: Shows alternative versions of the response
Shows a history of your edits
quiz.explanation: "Show drafts" reveals alternative versions of Gemini's response — you can pick the one that best fits your needs.

lessons.title: How Gemini Thinks
lessons.subtitle: Understanding the AI behind the magic

cards.headline: The more you understand how it works, the better your results
cards.body: You don't need a computer science degree — but knowing the basics of how Gemini processes your words will make you dramatically better at getting useful answers. Think of it like understanding how a search engine works made you better at Googling.
cards.statLabel: better results with basic AI understanding

cards.headline: Gemini predicts the best next word
cards.body: At its core, Gemini works by predicting what words should come next based on patterns learned from massive amounts of text. But it's not just memorising — it understands relationships, context, and meaning.
bullets: Trained on trillions of words from books, websites, and documents
Learns patterns and relationships, not just facts
Each response is generated fresh (not copy-pasted from the internet)
Can make mistakes — it's predicting, not looking things up

cards.headline: Context is everything
cards.body: Gemini reads your entire conversation when generating each response. This "context window" is like its short-term memory — and Gemini's is one of the largest available.
bullets: Gemini can hold very long conversations (up to 1 million tokens)
More context = better, more relevant answers
Starting a new chat resets the context completely
Long conversations stay coherent better than with other AIs

cards.headline: What Gemini CAN'T do
cards.body: Understanding limitations is just as important as knowing capabilities. Gemini is powerful but not perfect.
bullets: Can't browse the web in real-time (but has very recent training data)
May "hallucinate" — confidently state things that aren't true
Doesn't remember you between separate conversations
Can't take actions in the real world (send emails, make purchases)

cards.headline: Test the limits
cards.body: Try asking Gemini: "What happened in the news today?" — notice how it handles real-time information. Then try: "What's 847 × 293?" and check if it's right (answer: 248,171). This shows you where AI is strong and where to double-check.

quiz.question: How does Gemini generate its responses?
options: By searching the internet in real-time
By predicting the best words based on learned patterns
By copying from a database of pre-written answers
By asking other AI models for help
quiz.explanation: Gemini generates responses by predicting what words should come next, based on patterns and relationships it learned during training on massive amounts of text.

quiz.question: Gemini always provides 100% accurate information.
quiz.explanation: False. Gemini can "hallucinate" — generating confident-sounding responses that contain errors. Always verify critical facts.

quiz.question: What is a "context window" in AI?
options: The browser window where you use Gemini
The amount of conversation the AI can remember at once
A setting you configure in preferences
The time limit for each session
quiz.explanation: The context window is how much text (your conversation history) the AI can "see" when generating each response. Gemini's context window is one of the largest — up to 1 million tokens.

lessons.title: Writing Better Prompts
lessons.subtitle: The formula for clear prompts that get great answers every time

cards.headline: The difference between a good answer and a great answer? Your prompt.
cards.body: Most people type vague questions and get vague answers. Today you'll learn the simple formula that turns Gemini from "kinda useful" into "I can't believe how good this is." It takes 10 extra seconds of effort.
cards.statLabel: extra effort for dramatically better results

cards.headline: The 3-part prompt formula
cards.body: Every great prompt has three ingredients: Role + Task + Format. Tell Gemini WHO to be, WHAT to do, and HOW to present it.
bullets: Role: "Act as a senior marketing manager…"
Task: "…write a LinkedIn post announcing our new product…"
Format: "…in 150 words, with a hook opening and 3 bullet points"
Example: "Act as a nutritionist. Create a 7-day meal plan for someone trying to eat healthier on a budget. Format as a table with breakfast, lunch, and dinner."

cards.headline: Be specific, not vague
cards.body: The more detail you provide, the better Gemini can help. Compare these two prompts:
bullets: Vague: "Write me an email" → generic, unhelpful
Specific: "Write a friendly email to my team announcing Friday is a half-day, thank them for a great quarter, and remind them about the team lunch on Monday" → perfect result
Include: who it's for, what tone, how long, what to include
Think: "If I gave this instruction to a new employee, would they know exactly what to do?"

cards.headline: Power modifiers that improve any prompt
cards.body: Add these phrases to the end of almost any prompt for instant upgrades:
bullets: "Keep it under [X] words" — controls length
"Use simple language a 12-year-old would understand" — controls complexity
"Give me 3 options to choose from" — gets variety
"Format as bullet points / a table / numbered steps" — controls structure

cards.headline: Upgrade a basic prompt
cards.body: Take this basic prompt: "Give me workout ideas." Now rewrite it using the 3-part formula. For example: "Act as a personal trainer. Create a 20-minute home workout for a beginner with no equipment. Format as numbered steps with rest times between each exercise." Compare both results in Gemini.

quiz.question: What are the 3 parts of a great prompt?
quiz.explanation: The 3-part prompt formula is Role (who Gemini should act as) + Task (what to do) + Format (how to present it). This combination dramatically improves output quality.

quiz.question: Vague prompts produce better results because Gemini has more creative freedom.
quiz.explanation: False! Specific prompts with clear context always produce better results. Vague prompts lead to generic, often unhelpful responses.

quiz.question: Which power modifier controls the length of Gemini's response?
quiz.explanation: "Keep it under X words" directly controls response length. It's one of the most useful modifiers because AI tends to be verbose by default.

lessons.title: Conversations vs. Single Prompts
lessons.subtitle: When to keep chatting and when to start fresh

cards.headline: One of the most common mistakes? Using one long conversation for everything.
cards.body: Knowing when to continue a conversation and when to start a new one is a subtle skill that separates casual users from power users. Get this right and Gemini becomes dramatically more useful.
cards.statLabel: of users never start a new chat (and get worse results)

cards.headline: When to keep the conversation going
cards.body: Multi-turn conversations are powerful when you're building on a topic or iterating on a piece of work.
bullets: Refining a draft: "Make it more formal" → "Add a PS about the deadline"
Exploring a topic deeply: ask follow-ups, get clarification
Working on a project: Gemini remembers earlier decisions
Giving feedback: "That's good but change X" works perfectly

cards.headline: When to start fresh
cards.body: New conversations give Gemini a clean slate — which is often exactly what you want.
bullets: Switching topics entirely (don't mix recipe ideas with work emails)
When answers start getting confused or repetitive
For quick one-off questions ("What's the capital of Peru?")
When you want a completely different perspective on something

cards.headline: Managing your conversation history
cards.body: Gemini saves your conversations in a sidebar. Here's how to stay organised:
bullets: Pin important conversations you'll return to
Delete one-off chats to keep things clean
Rename conversations (click the title) so you can find them later
Think of each conversation as a "project folder"

cards.headline: Practice both approaches
cards.body: Start a multi-turn conversation: ask Gemini to write a short bio for you, then refine it over 3-4 messages ("Make it more casual", "Add that I love hiking", "Shorten to 2 sentences"). Then start a NEW conversation and ask a completely unrelated question. Notice how clean and focused the fresh start feels.

quiz.question: When should you start a new conversation instead of continuing?
options: When you want to refine a draft
When switching to a completely different topic
When you need follow-up information on the same topic
When giving feedback on a response
quiz.explanation: Start a new conversation when switching to a completely different topic. Mixing unrelated subjects in one chat confuses the AI and degrades response quality.

quiz.question: Gemini remembers your previous conversations when you start a new chat.
quiz.explanation: False. Each new conversation starts with a completely clean context. Gemini doesn't carry information between separate chats.

quiz.question: What's a good strategy for organising Gemini conversations?
options: Pin important ones and rename them clearly
Start a new chat after every single message
quiz.explanation: Pinning important conversations and renaming them clearly helps you find past work quickly. Think of each conversation as a project folder.

lessons.title: Gemini Free vs. Advanced
lessons.subtitle: What you get for free and when the upgrade is worth it

cards.headline: The free version is surprisingly powerful — but the paid tier is a game-changer
cards.body: Google offers Gemini in two tiers: a generous free version and Gemini Advanced (part of Google One AI Premium). Knowing what's in each tier helps you decide if and when to upgrade.
cards.statLabel: for Gemini Advanced (includes 2TB Google One storage)

cards.headline: What you get for free
cards.body: The free tier of Gemini is more capable than many paid AI tools. Here's what's included:
bullets: Full conversational AI with Gemini 1.5 Flash model
Image understanding — upload photos and get analysis
Integration with Google Search for current information
Conversation history and organisation

cards.headline: What Gemini Advanced adds
cards.body: The paid tier unlocks the most powerful model and exclusive features:
bullets: Gemini 2.5 Pro — significantly smarter for complex reasoning
Gems — custom AI assistants you build for specific tasks
1 million token context window (vs shorter free tier)
Priority access during peak times + early feature access

cards.headline: Who should upgrade?
cards.body: The free tier is perfect for most people getting started. Consider upgrading when:
bullets: You use Gemini daily for work tasks
You need longer, more complex conversations
You want custom Gems for repeated tasks
You already pay for Google One storage (bundled value)

cards.headline: Evaluate your needs
cards.body: Use Gemini free for the rest of this course. At the end, you'll know exactly which features matter to you. For now, ask Gemini: "What are the differences between Gemini free and Gemini Advanced?" and compare its answer to what you just learned.

quiz.question: What model does Gemini Advanced give you access to?
quiz.explanation: Gemini Advanced gives access to Gemini 2.5 Pro — Google's most capable model for complex reasoning, coding, and creative tasks.

quiz.question: The free version of Gemini can understand images you upload.
quiz.explanation: True! Even the free tier supports image understanding — you can upload photos and ask Gemini to analyse, describe, or answer questions about them.

quiz.question: What are "Gems" in Gemini Advanced?
options: Custom AI assistants you build for specific tasks
quiz.explanation: Gems are custom AI assistants you create in Gemini Advanced. You configure them for specific tasks (like a writing coach or code reviewer) and reuse them anytime.

lessons.title: Your Gemini Routine
lessons.subtitle: Building a daily habit with the 5 tasks Gemini handles best

cards.headline: The people who get the most from AI aren't the smartest — they're the most consistent
cards.body: After 6 days, you know what Gemini can do. Today's lesson is about making it a habit. The goal: reach for Gemini before Google for at least 5 tasks every day. Within a week, it'll feel as natural as opening your email.
cards.statLabel: per day to build an unbreakable AI habit

cards.headline: The 5 daily Gemini tasks
cards.body: These are the five things Gemini does faster and better than any other tool — make them your daily defaults:
bullets: 1. Morning briefing — "What should I know about [topic/industry] today?"
2. Email drafting — "Write a reply to this email that…"
3. Quick research — "Explain [concept] and give me the key takeaways"
4. Decision support — "Help me decide between A and B, given…"
5. End-of-day reflection — "Summarise what I worked on today into 3 bullet points"

cards.headline: The "Gemini First" rule
cards.body: Before opening Google, before asking a colleague, before spending 20 minutes figuring it out yourself — ask Gemini first. Even if it can't solve everything, it gives you a head start.
bullets: Writing anything? Draft it in Gemini first, then polish
Stuck on a decision? Ask Gemini for a pros/cons breakdown
Learning something new? Ask Gemini to explain it simply
Planning anything? Get Gemini to create the first outline

cards.headline: Tracking your progress
cards.body: Keep a simple tally this week. How many times did you use Gemini instead of doing it the old way?
bullets: Aim for 5 uses per day minimum
Note which tasks it saved the most time on
Notice when the old habits pull you back
Celebrate the time you saved — add it up at the end of the week

cards.headline: Set up your routine
cards.body: Right now, open Gemini and type: "Help me create a daily routine for using AI. I work in [your field] and my main tasks are [list 3-4 things you do daily]. Suggest 5 moments in my day where Gemini could save me time." Save that response — it's your personal AI routine.

quiz.question: What is the "Gemini First" rule?
options: Always use Gemini instead of Google Search
Ask Gemini before doing things the old way — get a head start
Always start your day with Gemini
quiz.explanation: The "Gemini First" rule means reaching for Gemini before spending time doing things manually. Even if it can't solve everything, it gives you a faster starting point.

quiz.question: You need to use Gemini for complex tasks to benefit from it.
quiz.explanation: False! The biggest time savings often come from simple, repeated tasks — drafting emails, quick research, and decision support. Consistency matters more than complexity.

quiz.question: How many daily Gemini tasks are recommended to build the habit?
quiz.explanation: 5 tasks per day is the sweet spot for building a consistent AI habit without feeling overwhelmed. It's enough to see real time savings.

lessons.title: Email & Messages
lessons.subtitle: Draft, reply, and polish emails in seconds

cards.headline: The average professional spends 28% of their workday on email
cards.body: That's over 2 hours every single day writing, reading, and replying to messages. Gemini can cut that in half — not by ignoring emails, but by drafting them in seconds instead of minutes.
cards.statLabel: spent on email daily by the average professional

cards.headline: Drafting emails from scratch
cards.body: Give Gemini the context and let it write the first draft. You just edit and send.
bullets: "Write a professional email to [person] about [topic]. Tone: [friendly/formal/urgent]"
"Draft a follow-up email — I haven't heard back in 5 days, stay polite but firm"
"Write a cold outreach email introducing my service to potential clients"
Always specify: recipient, purpose, tone, and any key details to include

cards.headline: Replying to existing emails
cards.body: Paste the email you received and tell Gemini how to respond:
bullets: "Here's an email I received: [paste]. Write a polite reply accepting the meeting"
"Reply declining this invitation — I'm busy but suggest next week instead"
"This customer is upset. Write an empathetic reply that offers a solution"
Pro tip: paste the email and just say "Reply saying yes, I'm available Tuesday"

cards.headline: Polishing and improving messages
cards.body: Already written something but it doesn't sound right? Gemini is a brilliant editor.
bullets: "Make this more professional: [paste your draft]"
"Shorten this email to 3 sentences without losing the key points"
"Check this for grammar and tone — I'm emailing my CEO"
"Translate this email to [language] keeping the professional tone"

cards.headline: Draft a real email
cards.body: Think of an email you need to send today (or this week). Open Gemini and type: "Write a [tone] email to [who] about [what]. Include: [key points]. Keep it under 150 words." Compare the result to how long it would have taken you to write from scratch.

quiz.question: What should you always include when asking Gemini to draft an email?
options: The recipient, purpose, tone, and key details
quiz.explanation: For the best email drafts, always provide: who it's for, what it's about, what tone to use, and any specific details or points to include.

quiz.question: Gemini can help you reply to emails you've received by pasting them in.
quiz.explanation: True! Paste the email you received, tell Gemini how you want to respond, and it will draft an appropriate reply in seconds.

quiz.question: What's the best way to shorten a long email with Gemini?
options: Ask "Shorten this to X sentences without losing key points"
Start a new email from scratch
quiz.explanation: Asking Gemini to "shorten this to X sentences without losing the key points" gives you a concise version that preserves the essential information.

lessons.title: Research & Summarisation
lessons.subtitle: Get answers, compare sources, and summarise anything fast

cards.headline: Stop spending 30 minutes reading when Gemini can give you the answer in 30 seconds
cards.body: Whether it's understanding a complex topic, comparing options, or digesting a long document — Gemini turns hours of research into minutes. It won't replace deep reading, but it eliminates the 80% of research that's just finding the key facts.
cards.statLabel: of research time is finding facts (not understanding them)

cards.headline: Quick research prompts
cards.body: These prompt patterns turn Gemini into your personal research assistant:
bullets: "Explain [topic] in simple terms with the 5 most important facts"
"Compare [A] vs [B] — give me a table with pros, cons, and price"
"What are the current best practices for [topic] in 2024?"
"Give me a 2-minute summary of [concept] that I can explain to my team"

cards.headline: Summarising long content
cards.body: Got a long article, report, or document? Gemini can distil it down instantly.
bullets: Paste text and say "Summarise this in 5 bullet points"
"What are the key takeaways from this article?"
"Pull out the action items from this meeting transcript"
"Explain this legal/technical document in plain English"

cards.headline: Research with Google grounding
cards.body: Gemini can access Google Search to provide current, cited information:
bullets: Ask about recent events — Gemini will cite sources
Look for the "Google it" chip beneath responses for deeper research
Double-check claims by asking "Can you verify this with sources?"
For critical decisions, always cross-reference with primary sources

cards.headline: Research something you've been curious about
cards.body: Pick a topic you've been meaning to research (a product to buy, a concept to learn, a decision to make). Ask Gemini: "I'm researching [topic]. Give me: 1) A simple explanation, 2) The 3 most important things to know, 3) Common mistakes people make." Notice how much faster this is than Googling.

quiz.question: What's the most effective way to summarise a long document with Gemini?
options: Paste the text and ask for specific output like "5 bullet points"
Ask Gemini to read your email inbox
quiz.explanation: Pasting the text and requesting specific output format (like "5 bullet points" or "key takeaways") gives you a focused, useful summary every time.

quiz.question: Gemini can access Google Search to provide current information.
quiz.explanation: True! Gemini has Google Search grounding, meaning it can access current information and cite sources for recent events and facts.

quiz.question: When should you cross-reference Gemini's research with other sources?
options: For critical decisions and important facts
Only if Gemini says it's unsure
quiz.explanation: Always cross-reference with primary sources for critical decisions. While Gemini is helpful for research, it can make mistakes, especially with specific facts and figures.

lessons.title: Writing & Content Creation
lessons.subtitle: Blog posts, social media, scripts — in your voice

cards.headline: Writer's block is officially a thing of the past
cards.body: Whether it's a LinkedIn post, a blog article, a product description, or a video script — Gemini can create a solid first draft in under 60 seconds. Your job shifts from "writing from scratch" to "editing and adding your personal touch."
cards.statLabel: from blank page to solid first draft

cards.headline: Blog posts and articles
cards.body: Gemini excels at long-form content when you give it the right direction:
bullets: "Write a 600-word blog post about [topic] for [audience]. Tone: conversational and helpful"
"Create an outline for an article on [topic] with 5 main sections"
"Write an introduction that hooks the reader with a surprising statistic"
Pro tip: generate the outline first, approve it, then ask Gemini to write each section

cards.headline: Social media content
cards.body: Short-form content is where Gemini saves the most time per word:
bullets: "Write 5 LinkedIn posts about [topic] — professional but not boring"
"Create an Instagram caption for [describe your photo]. Include 5 relevant hashtags"
"Write a Twitter/X thread (7 tweets) explaining [concept] in simple terms"
"Repurpose this blog post into 3 social media posts for different platforms"

cards.headline: Finding your voice
cards.body: The biggest fear with AI writing: sounding generic. Here's how to keep your voice:
bullets: Paste examples of YOUR writing and say "Match this tone and style"
Specify personality traits: "Write like someone who's friendly, slightly sarcastic, and uses short sentences"
Always edit the final output — add personal anecdotes, remove clichés
Use Gemini for structure and ideas, add your humanity on top

cards.headline: Create content you actually need
cards.body: Pick something you need to write this week — a social post, blog intro, or email newsletter. Give Gemini: the topic, your audience, the tone, and length. Then ask for 3 different versions. Pick your favourite and edit it to sound like you.

quiz.question: What's the best approach for writing a long blog post with Gemini?
options: Ask for the entire article in one prompt
Generate an outline first, then write each section separately
Only use it for the conclusion
quiz.explanation: Breaking long content into steps (outline → approve → write sections) gives you more control and better results than trying to generate everything at once.

quiz.question: Gemini can match your personal writing style if you provide examples.
quiz.explanation: True! Pasting examples of your own writing and asking Gemini to "match this tone and style" helps it produce content that sounds like you, not a generic AI.

quiz.question: How can you make AI-generated content feel less generic?
options: Add personal anecdotes and edit out clichés
quiz.explanation: The best AI-assisted content uses Gemini for structure and ideas, then adds personal stories, specific examples, and removes generic phrases. The human touch is what makes it authentic.

lessons.title: Brainstorming & Ideation
lessons.subtitle: Generate ideas, explore angles, break creative blocks

cards.headline: Your best ideas don't come from staring at a blank page — they come from having options
cards.body: Gemini can generate 20 ideas in 10 seconds. That changes the game: instead of struggling to think of ONE idea, you're choosing the BEST idea from a list. Creativity becomes curation.
cards.statLabel: in 10 seconds — then pick the best one

cards.headline: Quantity-first brainstorming
cards.body: The secret to great ideas? Start with volume. Bad ideas lead to good ones.
bullets: "Give me 15 ideas for [project/topic]. Be creative — weird ideas welcome"
"I need a name for my [business/product/event]. Give me 20 options across different styles"
"What are 10 different angles I could take for a presentation about [topic]?"
Pro tip: ask for "unconventional" or "surprising" ideas to push beyond obvious answers

cards.headline: Building on ideas
cards.body: Once you spot a promising direction, ask Gemini to dig deeper:
bullets: "I like idea #3 and #7. Combine them and give me 5 variations"
"Take this concept and show me how it would work for [specific context]"
"What would this look like if we made it 10x bolder?"
"Play devil's advocate — what's wrong with this idea?"

cards.headline: Creative frameworks Gemini knows
cards.body: Ask Gemini to use specific creativity techniques for structured brainstorming:
bullets: "Use SCAMPER method on my product: [describe product]"
"Apply the 'What if?' technique to [challenge]"
"Use reverse brainstorming — how could I make [problem] worse?"
"Give me ideas using the random connection technique with [random word]"

cards.headline: Brainstorm something real
cards.body: Think of something you're stuck on — a project name, a content idea, a gift for someone, a business idea. Ask Gemini: "Give me 15 ideas for [your thing]. Include some safe options and some wild, unexpected ones." Pick your top 3 and ask Gemini to develop each one further.

quiz.question: What's the best brainstorming strategy with AI?
options: Ask for exactly one perfect idea
Generate many options first, then refine your favourites
Avoid creative ideas and stick to safe ones
quiz.explanation: The best approach is quantity first — generate many options, then pick the most promising ones and ask Gemini to develop them further. Volume leads to quality.

quiz.question: SCAMPER is a creativity technique Gemini can apply to your ideas.
quiz.explanation: True! SCAMPER (Substitute, Combine, Adapt, Modify, Put to other uses, Eliminate, Reverse) is a structured creativity technique that Gemini knows and can apply to any product or idea.

quiz.question: What should you do after finding a promising idea in Gemini's list?
options: Ask Gemini to develop it further with variations and details
Start a completely new brainstorming session
quiz.explanation: When you spot a promising idea, ask Gemini to dig deeper — develop variations, show how it works in your context, or combine it with other ideas. The conversation builds momentum.

lessons.title: Learning & Explaining
lessons.subtitle: Use Gemini as a personal tutor for any topic

cards.headline: Imagine having a patient tutor available 24/7 who can explain anything at your level
cards.body: Gemini never gets frustrated, never judges, and can explain the same concept 10 different ways until it clicks. Whether you're learning a new skill, preparing for a presentation, or helping your kids with homework — it's the ultimate learning companion.
cards.statLabel: patient tutor available anytime you need it

cards.headline: Learning new concepts
cards.body: The key is telling Gemini your current level and how you want it explained:
bullets: "Explain [topic] like I'm a complete beginner with zero background"
"I understand the basics of [X]. Now explain [advanced concept] building on that"
"Teach me [skill] step by step. Start with the absolute basics"
"I'm confused about [specific thing]. Explain it using an everyday analogy"

cards.headline: The Feynman technique with Gemini
cards.body: The best way to learn is to explain. Use Gemini to test your understanding:
bullets: "I'm going to explain [topic] to you. Tell me what I got wrong or missed"
"Quiz me on [subject] — start easy and get harder"
"I think [concept] works like [your explanation]. Is that right?"
"Give me 5 questions to test if I really understand [topic]"

cards.headline: Explaining to others
cards.body: Need to present something complex? Gemini helps you simplify:
bullets: "Help me explain [technical topic] to my non-technical boss"
"Create a 3-minute explanation of [topic] for a general audience"
"Give me 3 analogies I can use to explain [concept]"
"Write a simple FAQ about [topic] with 5 questions and short answers"

cards.headline: Learn something new right now
cards.body: Pick something you've always wanted to understand better — investing, coding, nutrition, history, anything. Ask Gemini: "Teach me [topic] from scratch. I have 5 minutes. Start with the single most important concept and build from there." Then ask one follow-up question.

quiz.question: What's the Feynman technique when used with Gemini?
options: Asking Gemini to write a physics paper
Explaining a concept to Gemini and asking it to check your understanding
Memorising Gemini's responses word for word
Reading long articles generated by Gemini
quiz.explanation: The Feynman technique means learning by explaining. With Gemini, you explain a concept in your own words and ask it to point out gaps or mistakes in your understanding.

quiz.question: You should tell Gemini your current knowledge level when asking it to explain something.
quiz.explanation: True! Telling Gemini your level (beginner, intermediate, expert) helps it calibrate the explanation to be useful rather than too simple or too complex.

quiz.question: Which prompt is best for understanding a complex topic?
options: "Explain quantum physics like I'm a beginner, using everyday analogies"
quiz.explanation: Specifying your level (beginner) and preferred format (everyday analogies) gives Gemini the context to explain it in a way that actually helps you understand.

lessons.title: Planning & Decision-Making
lessons.subtitle: Pros and cons, project plans, and structured thinking

cards.headline: Every decision you overthink is time you'll never get back
cards.body: Gemini won't make decisions for you — but it will structure your thinking so the right choice becomes obvious. From travel planning to career moves, it's like having a strategic advisor who can see all the angles instantly.
cards.statLabel: to get a complete pros/cons analysis

cards.headline: Decision frameworks
cards.body: Turn fuzzy decisions into clear ones with these prompts:
bullets: "I'm deciding between [A] and [B]. Give me pros, cons, and a recommendation based on [my priorities]"
"What are the risks and rewards of [decision]? What am I not thinking about?"
"Help me think through [decision] using the 10-10-10 framework (how will I feel in 10 minutes, 10 months, 10 years?)"
"I'm leaning toward [X]. Play devil's advocate and tell me why I shouldn't"

cards.headline: Project and event planning
cards.body: Gemini excels at breaking big plans into actionable steps:
bullets: "Create a week-by-week plan for [project] with clear milestones"
"Plan a [event type] for [number] people. Budget: [amount]. Include checklist and timeline"
"I need to [achieve goal] in [timeframe]. Break it into daily/weekly actions"
"What am I forgetting? Here's my plan for [X] — what are the gaps?"

cards.headline: Everyday planning wins
cards.body: Don't just use Gemini for big decisions — the small ones add up:
bullets: "Plan my meals for the week — healthy, quick, budget-friendly"
"Create a packing list for a 5-day business trip to London"
"I have 3 hours free Saturday. Suggest the best use of that time given [my goals]"
"Help me prioritise these 8 tasks for today — I can realistically do 4"

cards.headline: Make a decision you've been putting off
cards.body: Think of a decision you've been mulling over (big or small). Ask Gemini: "I'm trying to decide [your decision]. My priorities are [list 2-3 things that matter most]. Give me a structured analysis with pros, cons, risks, and your recommendation." Notice how seeing it laid out makes the choice clearer.

quiz.question: What's the most effective way to use Gemini for decisions?
options: Ask "What should I do?" without context
Provide your options, priorities, and ask for structured analysis
Let Gemini make the final decision
Only use it for unimportant choices
quiz.explanation: The best results come from providing your options, stating your priorities, and asking for structured analysis (pros, cons, risks). Gemini organises your thinking — you make the final call.

quiz.question: Gemini can help identify gaps and blind spots in your plans.
quiz.explanation: True! Asking "What am I forgetting?" or "What are the gaps in this plan?" is one of the most valuable ways to use Gemini — it can spot things you haven't considered.

quiz.question: What is the 10-10-10 framework?
options: A rating system for AI responses
Thinking about how you'll feel in 10 minutes, 10 months, and 10 years
quiz.explanation: The 10-10-10 framework helps with decisions by considering how you'll feel about the choice in 10 minutes, 10 months, and 10 years — giving you short, medium, and long-term perspective.

lessons.title: Images & Multimodal Input
lessons.subtitle: Upload photos, analyse visuals, and unlock Gemini's superpower

cards.headline: Most people don't know Gemini can SEE — and that changes everything
cards.body: Gemini isn't just a text chatbot. Upload a photo, screenshot, whiteboard, receipt, chart, or handwritten note — and it understands what it's looking at. This multimodal ability is one of its biggest advantages over other AI tools.
cards.statLabel: to upload any image and get instant analysis

cards.headline: What you can upload
cards.body: Almost any image works. Here are the most useful types:
bullets: Screenshots — ask Gemini to explain, fix, or extract info
Photos of documents — receipts, menus, signs in other languages
Whiteboard or handwritten notes — "Convert this to typed text"
Charts and graphs — "Explain what this data shows"

cards.headline: Powerful image prompts
cards.body: Combine your image with specific instructions for incredible results:
bullets: "What's in this image?" — basic description and analysis
"Extract all the text from this photo" — instant OCR
"This is a screenshot of an error message. Explain what's wrong and how to fix it"
"Translate the text in this photo from [language] to English"

cards.headline: Creative and practical uses
cards.body: Once you start thinking visually, the possibilities explode:
bullets: Photo of your fridge → "What can I cook with these ingredients?"
Screenshot of a spreadsheet → "Explain this data and spot trends"
Photo of a plant → "What plant is this? How do I care for it?"
Image of a room → "Suggest how to rearrange this space"

cards.headline: Upload your first image
cards.body: Take a photo of something nearby — your desk, a page from a book, a receipt, or a screenshot on your phone. Upload it to Gemini and ask: "Describe what you see and suggest 3 useful things you could help me with based on this image." You'll be surprised at how much it understands.

quiz.question: What is multimodal input in Gemini?
options: Uploading images alongside text for AI to process both
quiz.explanation: Multimodal means Gemini can process multiple types of input together — text AND images. You upload a photo and ask questions about it, combining visual and text understanding.

quiz.question: Gemini can extract text from a photo of a handwritten note.
quiz.explanation: True! Gemini can read and transcribe handwritten notes, printed documents, signs, and any text visible in an image — like instant OCR.

quiz.question: Which is NOT something you can do with image uploads in Gemini?
options: Get cooking suggestions from a fridge photo
Translate text visible in an image
Send the image to your contacts
Explain what's happening in a chart
quiz.explanation: Gemini can analyse, describe, translate, and extract information from images — but it cannot take actions like sending images to your contacts.

lessons.title: Gems — Custom AI Assistants
lessons.subtitle: Create reusable AI experts for your specific tasks

cards.headline: What if you could clone your best prompts into permanent, one-click assistants?
cards.body: Gems are custom AI assistants you build inside Gemini. Instead of rewriting your best prompts every time, you create a Gem once — and it's always ready. Think of them as AI shortcuts for your most common tasks.
cards.statLabel: to activate your custom-built AI expert

cards.headline: What Gems are
cards.body: A Gem is a pre-configured Gemini persona with specific instructions, tone, and expertise:
bullets: Each Gem has a custom system prompt that shapes how it responds
You give it a name, description, and detailed instructions
Once created, it appears in your Gem library — always one click away
Gems remember their role across the entire conversation

cards.headline: Gem ideas that save hours
cards.body: Here are Gems that power users swear by:
bullets: Email Editor — "You polish my emails to be concise, professional, and warm"
Meeting Summariser — "I paste meeting notes, you extract action items and decisions"
Content Creator — "You write in my brand voice with my style guidelines"
Code Explainer — "You explain code like I'm a non-developer who needs to understand the logic"

cards.headline: How to create a Gem
cards.body: Building a Gem takes about 2 minutes:
bullets: 1. Click "Gem manager" in the left sidebar (or navigate to gems.google.com)
2. Click "New Gem" and give it a name
3. Write instructions — be specific about role, tone, format, and rules
4. Test it with a sample prompt and refine

cards.headline: Design your first Gem
cards.body: Think of a task you do repeatedly. Ask Gemini: "Help me write instructions for a custom Gem that [describe what you want]. Include: the role it should play, the tone it should use, rules it must follow, and the format it should output." Save those instructions — you can use them to create your Gem.

quiz.question: What is a Gem in Gemini?
options: A custom AI assistant with pre-configured instructions
A premium feature that costs extra
quiz.explanation: A Gem is a custom AI assistant you create with specific instructions, role, and tone. Once built, it's always available in your library for one-click access.

quiz.question: Gems remember their configured role throughout the entire conversation.
quiz.explanation: True! Unlike regular prompts that can drift, Gems maintain their configured persona and instructions across the entire conversation.

quiz.question: How long does it typically take to create a Gem?
options: You need to apply and wait for approval
quiz.explanation: Creating a Gem takes about 2 minutes — name it, write clear instructions, and test with a sample prompt. No coding or approval needed.

lessons.title: Gemini in Google Workspace
lessons.subtitle: AI inside Gmail, Docs, Sheets, Slides, and Meet

cards.headline: The real magic happens when AI meets the tools you already use every day
cards.body: Gemini isn't just at gemini.google.com — it's embedded directly inside Gmail, Google Docs, Sheets, Slides, and Meet. No copy-pasting between tabs. No switching apps. AI right where you work.
cards.statLabel: to switch — Gemini works inside your existing tools

cards.headline: Gemini in Gmail
cards.body: Look for the "Help me write" button when composing emails:
bullets: "Help me write" generates a full draft from a brief description
Highlight text and choose "Refine" to polish or shorten
"Summarise this email" in long threads — instant catch-up
Smart Reply suggestions get better with Gemini behind them

cards.headline: Gemini in Google Docs
cards.body: The side panel and inline tools transform how you write:
bullets: Type "@" and select Gemini to insert AI-generated content inline
Highlight text → "Help me write" to rewrite, expand, or summarise
Side panel: ask questions about your document ("What are the key points?")
Generate entire first drafts: "Write a project proposal for…"

cards.headline: Gemini in Slides and Meet
cards.body: Presentations and meetings get a major upgrade too:
bullets: Slides: "Create a slide about…" generates layout, text, and imagery
Slides: "Generate an image of…" for custom visuals without stock photos
Meet: Real-time transcription and "Summarise what I missed"
Meet: "Take notes for me" creates action items automatically

cards.headline: Try it in a Google Doc
cards.body: Open a new Google Doc. Type a sentence or two about something you're working on. Then highlight the text and look for the "Help me write" option (or try typing "@Gemini" if available in your workspace). Ask it to expand your notes into a full paragraph. See how seamlessly it works without leaving your document.

quiz.question: Where can you find Gemini inside Gmail?
options: The "Help me write" button when composing emails
quiz.explanation: In Gmail, Gemini appears as the "Help me write" button when you're composing or replying to emails. It can draft, refine, and shorten messages right inside your email.

quiz.question: Gemini in Google Meet can summarise what you missed if you join late.
quiz.explanation: True! Gemini in Google Meet can provide meeting summaries, transcriptions, and even highlight action items — perfect for catching up if you joined late.

quiz.question: How do you access Gemini inside Google Docs?
options: Use the side panel or highlight text and select "Help me write"
It only works in the mobile app
You need to enable developer mode
quiz.explanation: In Google Docs, Gemini is available through the side panel (for asking questions) and inline through "Help me write" (highlight text or use the @ menu to generate content).

lessons.title: Google Sheets + Gemini
lessons.subtitle: Formulas, data analysis, and insights from spreadsheets

cards.headline: Spreadsheets just went from intimidating to effortless
cards.body: If you've ever stared at a spreadsheet wondering which formula to use, those days are over. Gemini can write formulas, explain data, create charts, and spot trends — all from plain English instructions.
cards.statLabel: complex formulas you'll never need to memorise again

cards.headline: Gemini for formulas
cards.body: Stop Googling "how to VLOOKUP" — just describe what you want:
bullets: "Write a formula that adds all values in column B where column A says 'Sales'"
"I need a formula to calculate the percentage change between B2 and B3"
"Create a VLOOKUP that finds a product name in Sheet2 based on the ID in A1"
Paste your formula and ask "Explain what this formula does" to understand existing work

cards.headline: Data analysis in plain English
cards.body: Use the Gemini side panel in Sheets to ask questions about your data:
bullets: "What are the trends in this data?"
"Which product category has the highest growth?"
"Create a chart showing monthly revenue over time"
"Highlight all rows where the value in column C is below average"

cards.headline: Automating repetitive spreadsheet tasks
cards.body: Gemini handles the boring parts of spreadsheet work:
bullets: "Clean this data — remove duplicates and fix inconsistent capitalisation"
"Generate sample data for testing — 50 rows of fake customer names, emails, and order amounts"
"Convert this data into a pivot table summary"
"Create conditional formatting: green if positive, red if negative"

cards.headline: Get Gemini to help with a real spreadsheet
cards.body: Open any Google Sheet (or create a new one with some sample numbers). Open the Gemini side panel and ask: "Look at my data and tell me something interesting." Or paste a formula you don't understand into Gemini and ask it to explain. Either way — you'll see how it transforms spreadsheet work.

quiz.question: How can Gemini help with spreadsheet formulas?
options: It can only explain formulas, not write them
You describe what you need in plain English and it writes the formula
It only works with basic SUM formulas
You need to know the formula name first
quiz.explanation: Gemini can write complex formulas from plain English descriptions — just describe what you want to calculate and it generates the correct formula for you.

quiz.question: Gemini can create charts from your spreadsheet data.
quiz.explanation: True! Gemini in Google Sheets can create charts, identify trends, and visualise your data — all from natural language requests.

quiz.question: What's the best way to understand someone else's complex formula?
options: Paste it into Gemini and ask "Explain what this formula does"
Ignore it and work around it
quiz.explanation: Pasting a complex formula into Gemini and asking for an explanation gives you a plain-English breakdown of what each part does — much faster than decoding it yourself.

lessons.title: Extensions & Connected Tools
lessons.subtitle: Google Flights, Hotels, Maps, YouTube — live data at your fingertips

cards.headline: Gemini doesn't just know things — it can look things up for you in real time
cards.body: Extensions connect Gemini to live Google services. Need a flight price? Hotel availability? YouTube video recommendation? Directions? Gemini pulls real data from these services directly into your conversation.
cards.statLabel: Google services Gemini can access live

cards.headline: What extensions are
cards.body: Extensions are built-in connections between Gemini and other Google services:
bullets: Google Flights — search real flight prices and routes
Google Hotels — find accommodation with availability and pricing
Google Maps — get directions, find places, estimate travel times
YouTube — find and summarise videos on any topic

cards.headline: How to use extensions
cards.body: You don't need to "activate" anything — just ask naturally and Gemini uses the right extension:
bullets: "Find flights from London to Barcelona next weekend under £200"
"Show me hotels near Times Square for 2 nights in August"
"How long does it take to drive from Manchester to Edinburgh?"
"Find me a YouTube video that explains how mortgages work"

cards.headline: Google Workspace extensions
cards.body: Gemini can also connect to your personal Google data (when enabled):
bullets: Gmail — "Find the email from Sarah about the project deadline"
Google Drive — "Summarise the document called Q3 Report in my Drive"
Google Calendar — "What's on my schedule tomorrow?"
You control which extensions are active in Settings → Extensions

cards.headline: Try a live search
cards.body: Ask Gemini something that requires live data: "Find me return flights from [your city] to [a destination] for [upcoming dates]. Show me the cheapest options." Watch how it pulls real pricing from Google Flights. Then try: "Now find a hotel near the city centre for those dates."

quiz.question: What are Gemini extensions?
options: Third-party apps you install from a store
Built-in connections to live Google services like Flights and Maps
quiz.explanation: Extensions are built-in connections between Gemini and Google services (Flights, Hotels, Maps, YouTube, Gmail, Drive, Calendar). They provide live, real data directly in your conversation.

quiz.question: You need to manually activate extensions before Gemini can use them.
quiz.explanation: False! Most extensions work automatically — just ask naturally and Gemini detects which service to query. You can manage which ones are enabled in Settings, but they work by default.

quiz.question: Which of these can Gemini's extensions do?
options: Book and pay for a flight automatically
Search real flight prices and hotel availability
Make phone calls on your behalf
quiz.explanation: Gemini extensions can search and display real data (flight prices, hotel availability, directions) but cannot take actions like booking or making payments on your behalf.

lessons.title: Advanced Prompting Techniques
lessons.subtitle: Chain-of-thought, role prompts, few-shot examples, and output formatting

cards.headline: The gap between a good AI user and a great one? These 4 techniques.
cards.body: You already know the basics. Now it's time for the techniques that professionals use to get consistently excellent results. These aren't tricks — they're fundamental patterns that work because of how AI processes information.
cards.statLabel: that transform your results from good to exceptional

cards.headline: Chain-of-thought prompting
cards.body: Ask Gemini to think step by step before answering — this dramatically improves accuracy for complex questions.
bullets: "Think through this step by step before giving your final answer"
"Walk me through your reasoning, then give a conclusion"
"Break this problem into parts and solve each one"
Works best for: maths, logic, strategy, analysis, and complex decisions

cards.headline: Few-shot examples
cards.body: Show Gemini exactly what you want by providing examples of the input/output pattern:
bullets: "Here are 3 examples of the format I want: [example 1], [example 2], [example 3]. Now do the same for: [your input]"
Works brilliantly for consistent formatting across multiple items
Great for: product descriptions, review responses, social posts, data extraction
The more examples you give, the more consistent the output

cards.headline: Structured output formatting
cards.body: Control exactly how Gemini presents information:
bullets: "Respond in JSON format with keys: title, summary, action_items"
"Format as a table with columns: Feature, Free Tier, Paid Tier"
"Give me exactly 5 bullet points, each under 15 words"
"Structure your response as: Problem → Cause → Solution → Prevention"

cards.headline: Apply advanced techniques
cards.body: Try chain-of-thought: "I'm considering starting a side business selling [product]. Think through step by step: Is there demand? What would it cost to start? What are the risks? What's my realistic timeline to profit? Give me your final recommendation." Notice how much richer the analysis is compared to just asking "Should I start this business?"

quiz.question: What does chain-of-thought prompting do?
options: Asks Gemini to reason step by step before answering
Creates a chain of multiple conversations
quiz.explanation: Chain-of-thought prompting asks Gemini to think through a problem step by step before giving its final answer. This dramatically improves accuracy for complex reasoning tasks.

quiz.question: Few-shot examples help Gemini produce more consistent output formatting.
quiz.explanation: True! Providing examples of your desired input/output pattern helps Gemini replicate that exact format consistently — perfect for batch tasks like product descriptions or data extraction.

quiz.question: Which technique is best for getting Gemini to output data in a specific structure?
options: Specifying the exact format (JSON, table, specific structure)
quiz.explanation: Structured output formatting — explicitly telling Gemini the format you want (JSON, table, numbered list, specific template) — gives you precise control over how information is presented.

lessons.title: Building AI Workflows
lessons.subtitle: Multi-step processes — research, draft, edit, publish

cards.headline: Individual prompts are useful. Workflows are transformational.
cards.body: A workflow is a sequence of prompts that build on each other to complete a complex task end-to-end. Instead of "write me an email," think "research this person → find a connection point → draft a personalised outreach → create 3 variations → pick the best one."
cards.statLabel: more value from multi-step workflows vs single prompts

cards.headline: The workflow mindset
cards.body: Think of complex tasks as pipelines where each step feeds the next:
bullets: Step 1: Research/gather information ("Tell me about…")
Step 2: Analyse/structure ("Based on that, what's the best approach for…")
Step 3: Create/draft ("Now write…")
Step 4: Refine/polish ("Make it more… / Change the…")

cards.headline: Example workflows
cards.body: Here are complete workflows you can use immediately:
bullets: Content workflow: Research topic → outline article → write draft → edit for tone → create social snippets
Decision workflow: Define options → research each → compare (table) → recommend → action plan
Meeting workflow: Review agenda → prepare talking points → draft follow-up email → create action items
Learning workflow: Explain concept → quiz me → identify gaps → teach those gaps → test again

cards.headline: Workflow tips for power users
cards.body: These tips make workflows faster and more reliable:
bullets: Keep it in one conversation — Gemini uses earlier context
Label your steps: "Step 1:" "Step 2:" so the AI tracks the sequence
Save your best workflows as templates (or build them into Gems)
If a step goes wrong, just say "Let's redo Step 3 with different…"

cards.headline: Run your first workflow
cards.body: Try this 4-step content workflow in one conversation: 1) "Research the top 5 benefits of [topic you know about]" 2) "Create an outline for a LinkedIn post using the most surprising benefit" 3) "Write the post in a conversational, professional tone — 200 words max" 4) "Give me 3 alternative hooks for the opening line." You just created better content than most people do in an hour.

quiz.question: What is an AI workflow?
options: A single prompt that does everything at once
A sequence of prompts that build on each other to complete a complex task
quiz.explanation: An AI workflow is a sequence of prompts in one conversation where each step builds on the previous output — research → analyse → create → refine. This produces much better results than trying to do everything in one prompt.

quiz.question: You should keep all workflow steps in the same conversation.
quiz.explanation: True! Keeping workflow steps in one conversation lets Gemini use context from earlier steps. Each response builds on what came before, creating a coherent end-to-end output.

quiz.question: What should you do if one step in your workflow goes wrong?
options: Accept the bad output and move on
Ask Gemini to redo that specific step with adjusted instructions
Switch to a different AI tool
quiz.explanation: Simply ask Gemini to redo the specific step that went wrong — "Let's redo Step 3 with a more formal tone." No need to restart the entire workflow.

lessons.title: Your Gemini Operating System
lessons.subtitle: Combine everything into a personal productivity system

cards.headline: Congratulations — you're no longer a beginner. You're a Gemini power user.
cards.body: Over the past 20 days, you've learned prompting, multimodal input, Workspace integration, Gems, extensions, workflows, and advanced techniques. Today, you'll combine everything into a personal system that saves you hours every week — permanently.
cards.statLabel: saved per week with a complete Gemini system

cards.headline: Your Gemini operating system
cards.body: A personal AI operating system has 4 layers. You now have all the skills to build each one:
bullets: 1. Daily defaults — the 5 tasks you always do with Gemini (email, research, writing, planning, learning)
2. Custom Gems — pre-built assistants for your recurring tasks
3. Workflows — multi-step templates for complex projects
4. Workspace integration — AI inside the tools you already use

cards.headline: Building your Gem library
cards.body: Power users have 5-10 Gems covering their most common needs:
bullets: Work Gems: Email Writer, Meeting Prep, Report Summariser
Creative Gems: Content Creator (in your voice), Brainstorm Partner
Personal Gems: Meal Planner, Trip Planner, Learning Coach
Start with 3 Gems this week — add more as you discover patterns

cards.headline: Staying ahead of the curve
cards.body: Gemini evolves fast. Here's how to keep your skills current:
bullets: Follow Google's AI blog for new feature announcements
Try new features the day they launch — early adopters gain the most
Revisit your Gems monthly — update instructions as you learn what works
Share what works with your team — multiplied time savings

cards.headline: Design your system
cards.body: Ask Gemini: "Help me design my personal AI operating system. I work in [your field] and my biggest time sinks are [list 3-4 things]. Based on everything Gemini can do — daily prompts, Gems, workflows, and Workspace features — create a personalised system that saves me maximum time each week. Format as a one-page cheat sheet I can print." Save this — it's your ongoing reference.

quiz.question: What are the 4 layers of a Gemini operating system?
options: Daily defaults, custom Gems, workflows, Workspace integration
Free tier, paid tier, enterprise, developer
quiz.explanation: A complete Gemini operating system has 4 layers: Daily defaults (routine tasks), Custom Gems (pre-built assistants), Workflows (multi-step templates), and Workspace integration (AI inside your existing tools).

quiz.question: Power users typically have 5-10 custom Gems for their most common tasks.
quiz.explanation: True! Having 5-10 Gems covering your most frequent tasks means one-click access to perfectly configured AI assistants for emails, content, planning, and more.

quiz.question: How often should you update your Gems?
options: Monthly — refine instructions based on what works
quiz.explanation: Revisiting your Gems monthly lets you refine their instructions based on what's working and what isn't. As you learn more about prompting, your Gems get better too.
